analysis:
The PR changes operator-facing CLI diagnostic wording and adds a small status helper. DoctorRunner.swift lines 223 and 241 now say counters are daemon-process-scoped, count output tokens, and point to the console Earnings page for paid work. StatusCommand.swift line 175 now calls the new Status.servedRequestLines (StatusCommand+ServedRequests.swift lines 10-24), which prints the served count, output tokens and daemon uptime, and conditionally the stats.cancellationsPartialComplete count. Tests are updated to match the new strings.

Security review: the helper only reads the already-local DaemonState (stats, uptime). It makes no network calls, spawns no processes, parses no untrusted input, and writes no files. It outputs only aggregate counters and no prompts, keys, tokens or machine identifiers (A-001, A-003, A-008 and A-010 are not touched). No authorization, attestation (TB-009/TB-011), WebSocket (TB-002), prefix-cache (T-041) or add-on hold (TB-012) logic changed. The wording is more accurate: it no longer implies the counts are paid or reported to the coordinator, and it avoids overclaiming, which is consistent with T-056's concern about overclaiming. Fields are formatted with plain string interpolation, and the state file is local and owner-controlled, so there is no meaningful injection surface beyond the terminal output the user already controls.

Open questions: whether DaemonState.stats.cancellationsPartialComplete exists as an optional Int in ProviderCore, which this diff does not show; a mismatch would only cause a compile error, not a security issue. Whether compactDuration is accessible from the extension is also not visible and is likewise a build matter. No findings.
